en.headline: Customs arrest 61-year-old over counterfeit perfume operation involving HK$6 million
en.dek: A father was held after officers raided a Kwun Tong unit last week and seized about 800 suspected fake luxury items; his son remains overseas.
body: The Customs and Excise Department said it had dismantled two online stores and a distribution centre in Kwun Tong suspected of selling counterfeit perfumes and designer figurines. A 61-year-old man was arrested and released on bail while investigators continue to seek his 30-year-old son, who is alleged to have run the business from overseas.

Officers raided an industrial unit on 11 November after a public tip and assistance from trademark owners. They seized about 800 items with an estimated market value of HK$500,000. Customs said the operation had generated roughly HK$6 million in proceeds over recent years and that the arrested man had handled daily storage and dispatch.

Inspector Liu Man-chun of the Copyright and Trademark Technology Crime Investigation Group said the counterfeit perfumes cost HK$100 to HK$200 each and were sold for HK$700 to HK$1,000, about 80 per cent of genuine prices. Genuine bottles have centred labels and clear base engravings; the fakes do not. Samples will be sent to the Government Laboratory for safety testing because of poor storage conditions.
Customs has frozen about HK$2.5 million in related assets. The department warned the public against buying from suspicious online outlets and said further arrests were possible.

zh.headline: 海關破觀塘網店售冒牌香水案 拘61歲父親 兒子在逃
zh.dek: 海關上周三突擊觀塘工廈單位，檢獲約800件懷疑冒牌香水及公仔，涉犯罪得益約600萬元。
body: 香港海關表示，已搗破兩間網上店舖及觀塘一個分銷中心，涉嫌售賣冒牌香水及潮玩公仔。一名61歲男子被捕，現正保釋候查；其30歲兒子被指為主謀，長期身在海外，調查仍在進行。
海關於本月11日接獲線報並在商標持有人協助下採取行動，在觀塘工廈單位檢獲約800件物品，估計市值約50萬元。當局指，涉案業務近年累積犯罪得益約600萬元，被捕男子負責日常儲存及發貨工作。
版權及商標科技罪案調查組調查主任廖聞晉表示，冒牌香水成本約100至200元，售價約700至1,000元，約為正貨八成。正貨樽身貼紙字體較正中、瓶底刻字清晰，冒牌貨則相反。因倉庫環境惡劣，海關稍後會將樣本送政府化驗所測試安全。
海關已凍結約250萬元涉案資產。當局提醒市民勿於可疑網店購物，並不排除進一步拘捕。
